ref: Leg. 30, final sentence of ch. 30 (Otto and ANF chapter numbers agree)
greek: Ὅτι μὲν οὖν οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἄθεοι, ϑεὸν ἄγοντες τὸν ποιητὴν τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς καὶ τὸν παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ λόγον, κατὰ δύναμιν τὴν ἐμὴν, εἰ καὶ μὴ πρὸς ἀξίαν, ἐλήλεγκται.
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 160; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: That, therefore, we are not atheists, acknowledging as we do God the Maker of this universe and His Logos, has been proved according to my ability, if not according to the importance of the subject.
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Christians deny atheism because they acknowledge God the Maker of the universe together with his Logos.
limits: Only two terms (God and the Logos) are named here, no Spirit. 'τὸν παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ λόγον' ('his Logos', from him) does not settle whether the Logos is a distinct hypostasis, a generated word, or the Son. The sentence names the Logos as an object of confession beside the Maker, but does not call it God.

ref: Leg. 30, Callimachus and Cretans passage (mid-chapter 30, before the 'Ὅτι μὲν οὖν' sentence)
greek: κἂν μὲν τὸ ἄντρον βλέπῃς, τὸν Ῥέας τόκον ὑπομιμνήσκῃ· ἂν δὲ τὴν σορὸν ἴδῃς, ἐπισκοτεῖς τῷ τεϑνηκότι, οὐκ εἰδὼς ὅτι μόνος ἀΐδιος [ὁ] ἀγένητος ϑεός.
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 158; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto; Apparatus n. 22 (p. 159, pdf 243) discusses ἀγέννητος vs ἀγένητος.
english: ...when you see the coffin, you throw a shadow over his death, not considering that the unbegotten God alone is eternal.
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Athenagoras says that the unbegotten God alone is eternal, in a polemic against tomb-cults of gods who were born and died.
limits: Literal words say 'alone eternal' (μόνος ἀΐδιος), which Arian and Unitarian readers set against an eternal Son. The Nicene answer is contextual: the sentence contrasts the eternity of God with gods born from men, and Leg. 10 gives an eternal Logos in God ('from the beginning God, being eternal mind, had the Logos in himself'). The article [ὁ] and the spelling ἀγένητος/ἀγέννητος are editorial variants (Otto apparatus n. 22, p. 159, pdf 243). Greek is OCR plus partial image check.

ref: Leg. 31, the 'God is witness by night and by day' sentence
greek: καὶ νύκτωρ καὶ μεϑ᾽ ἡμέραν τὸν ϑεὸν οἴδαμεν, πάντα δὲ φῶς αὐτὸν ὄντα καὶ τὰ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ἡμῶν ὁρᾶν
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 164; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: since we know that God is witness to what we think and what we say both by night and by day, and that He, being Himself light, sees all things in our heart
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: God knows the thoughts and words of Christians at all times, because he is light and sees the heart.
limits: Names God only; neither the Son nor the Spirit appears. Apparatus records Lubanensis reading σαφῶς for φῶς (Otto keeps φῶς). The sentence is about divine omniscience, so it does not decide the Trinitarian question either way.

ref: Leg. 31, the blessed life 'with God' (end of the resurrection-hope sentence)
greek: ὡς ἂν μετὰ ϑεοῦ καὶ σὺν ϑεῷ ἀκλινεῖς καὶ ἀπαϑεῖς τὴν ψυχήν, οὐχ ὡς σάρκες, κἂν ἔχωμεν, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς οὐράνιον πνεῦμα, μενοῦμεν
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 164; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: we shall abide near God, and with God, free from all change or suffering in the soul, not as flesh, even though we shall have flesh, but as heavenly spirit
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: The saved will abide with God (μετὰ θεοῦ, σὺν θεῷ) in a changeless state.
limits: Describes communion with God after death; no Son or Spirit is named. Otto's apparatus comments on the two prepositional phrases and on the particle ἂν; not read in full.

ref: Leg. 31, 'heavenly spirit' and 'God made us' (same passage as A6-04)
greek: ἀλλ᾽ ὡς οὐράνιον πνεῦμα, μενοῦμεν … οὐ γὰρ ἡμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἢ ὑποζύγια, πάρεργον καὶ ἵνα ἀπολοίμεϑα καὶ ἀφανισϑείημεν, ἔπλασεν ὁ ϑεός.
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 164; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: but as heavenly spirit ... for God has not made us as sheep or beasts of burden, a mere by-work, and that we should perish and be annihilated.
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: The blessed will be 'heavenly spirit' (not flesh); God made human beings for a purpose, not to perish.
limits: Here 'πνεῦμα' names the state of the risen human, not the Holy Spirit. No ἅγιον πνεῦμα occurs in Leg. 28-37. Nearby Leg. 10 and 12 carry the Spirit material (see other assignments).

ref: Leg. 32, opening claim of ch. 32 and 'the Logos again says to us' (ch. 32, before the kiss passage)
greek: ἐν ἀρχῇ δὲ ὑμῖν, δεσπόται, ϑεοδίδακτον εἶναι τὸν παρ᾽ ἡμᾶς λόγον ἐπιστάμην), ἀλλ᾽ ἔστιν ἡμῖν νόμος δικαιοσύνης μέτρον ἐποίησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ τοὺς πέλας ἔχειν. … πάλιν ἡμῖν λέγοντος τοῦ λόγου
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 168; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: at the outset I proved to you, sovereign lords, that our doctrine is from the teaching of God ... the Logos again says to us
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Christian ethical teaching is 'God-taught', and the Logos speaks it to Christians (Scripture or Christ's teaching).
limits: Here λόγος means the word or teaching (and in context Scripture), not explicitly the Son. The capital 'Logos' is Pratten's choice. The Matthew 5:28 and 19:9 citations are added by editors, not named in Athenagoras's Greek.

ref: Leg. 32, quotation of Matthew 5:28 with an unnamed speaker
greek: Οἷς οὖν μηδὲν τὸ πλέον ἔξεστιν ὁρᾶν ἢ ἐφ᾽ ἃ ἔπλασεν τοὺς ὀφϑαλμοὺς ὁ ϑεός, ἡμῖν φῶς αὐτοὺς εἶναι … Ὃ γὰρ βλέπων, φησί, γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιϑυμῆσαι αὐτῆς, ἤδη μεμοίχευκεν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 166; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: For, says He, he that looks on a woman to lust after her, has committed adultery already in his heart. Matthew 5:28
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Athenagoras quotes a gospel saying with 'φησί' (he says), without naming Jesus or Christ.
limits: NEGATIVE: the speaker is not named, so 'Jesus' and 'Christ' do not appear in this quotation or in the Legatio's Greek main text. The reference 'Matthew 5:28' is an editorial addition in ANF, not Athenagoras's text.

ref: Leg. 32, kinship language 'sons and daughters' (human kinship)
greek: Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡλικίαν υἱοὺς καὶ ϑυγατέρας [...] τοὺς δὲ ἀδελφοὺς ἔχομεν καὶ ἀδελφάς, καὶ τοῖς προβεβηκόσι τὴν τῶν πατέρων καὶ μητέρων τιμὴν ἀπονέμομεν.
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 168; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: according to age, we recognise some as sons and daughters, others we regard as brothers and sisters
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Christians use kinship terms (sons, daughters, brothers, sisters) for one another by age.
limits: Only the ordinary human sense of υἱός occurs here. This is one of the few 'son' words after Leg. 12 in this range. The verb is an OCR gap ([...]) and the form υἱοὺς is read from the OCR text layer.

ref: Leg. 33, God made one man and one woman (marriage ethics)
greek: καὶ εἰ τέϑνηκε, μοιχὸς ἐστι παρακεκαλυμμένος, παραβαίνων μὲν τὴν χεῖρα τοῦ ϑεοῦ, ὅτι ἐν ἀρχῇ ὁ ϑεὸς ἕνα ἄνδρα ἔπλασε καὶ μίαν γυναῖκα
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 174; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: because in the beginning God made one man and one woman
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: God alone is the creator of the first human pair; marriage is grounded in creation.
limits: God is the sole agent here. Otto's note on the same page explains 'the hand of God' as the formula for creation and cites Leg. 34 'χεῖρα καὶ γνώμην θεοῦ'. Athenagoras does not identify the hand with the Son or the Spirit, so no Irenaean 'two hands' reading is made in this passage.

ref: Leg. 34, beauty made by 'hand and will of God'
greek: τὸ ποιητὸν τοῦ ϑεοῦ καλόν (οὐ γὰρ ὃ αὐτοποίητον ἐπὶ γῆς τὸ κάλλος, ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ χειρὸς καὶ γνώμης πεμπόμενον τοῦ ϑεοῦ)
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 176; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: for beauty on earth is not self-made, but sent hither by the hand and will of God
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Earthly beauty is sent by God's hand and will, not self-made.
limits: 'Hand and will' (χειρὸς καὶ γνώμης) is a creation formula. It is not identified with the Son or the Spirit, so it does not by itself support a two-hands Trinitarian reading. Greek read from OCR; check the line against the scan.

ref: Leg. 35, 'account to God for the abortion' and the fœtus as God's creature
greek: λόγον ὑφέξειν τῆς ἐξαμβλώσεως τῷ ϑεῷ φαμεν, κατὰ ποῖον ἀνδροφονοῦμεν λόγον; Οὐ γὰρ τοῦ αὐτοῦ νομίζειν μὲν καὶ τὸ κατὰ γαστρὸς ζῷον εἶναι καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τοῦ μέλειν τῷ ϑεῷ
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 180; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: will have to give an account to God for the abortion, on what principle should we commit murder? For it does not belong to the same person to regard the very fœtus in the womb as a created being, and therefore an object of God's care
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Christians hold that the unborn child is God's creature and under God's care, and that the women who abort will answer to God.
limits: God alone is the judge and the one who cares. No Son or Spirit is named. Greek read from OCR; check against the scan.

ref: Leg. 36, nothing escapes God's scrutiny (resurrection and judgement)
greek: τοὺς δὲ μηδὲν ἀνεξέταστον ἔσεσθαι παρὰ τῷ ϑεῷ, συγκολασϑήσεσϑαι δὲ καὶ τὸ ὑπουργῆσαν σῶμα ταῖς ἀλόγοις ὅρμαῖς τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ ἐπιϑυμίαις πεπεισμένους
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 182; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: those who are persuaded that nothing will escape the scrutiny of God, but that even the body which has ministered to the irrational impulses of the soul, and to its desires, will be punished along with it
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: Those who believe in God's judgement and in the resurrection of the body will avoid sin.
limits: God alone is the judge; no Son or Spirit is named. Ch. 36 begins on p. 180 (pdf 264); the exact start of ch. 36 was not checked. Greek read from OCR; check against the scan.

ref: Leg. 37, 'pious' rulers and the imperial 'son' (παῖς) who succeeds his father
greek: καὶ ϑεοσεβεῖς καὶ ἐπιεικεῖς καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς κεκολασμένοι, τὴν βασιλικὴν κεφαλὴν ἐπινεύσατε … ἵνα παῖς μὲν παρὰ πατρὸς κατὰ τὸ δικαιότατον διαδέχησϑε τὴν βασιλείαν
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi VII (Jena: Mauke, 1857), p. 184; Otto 1857 scan (archive.org athenagoraephilo00athe), PDF text layer read at the printed page; Greek ϑ kept as printed by Otto
english: that you may, as is most equitable, receive the kingdom, son from father
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2; New Advent text, revised by Kevin Knight)
page: page unknown (New Advent web text, no ANF page numbers)
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe (Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885); web text at newadvent.org
what_it_says: The prayer that the emperors, pious and gentle, succeed their father in the kingdom (Marcus to Commodus).
limits: NEGATIVE for the 'Son' question: the only 'son' word in Leg. 28-37 here (παῖς) means the imperial heir; the Greek has no υἱός and no 'Son of God'. Apparatus n. 4 (p. 185) records a Mon. variant and a later correction above the line; Otto keeps παῖς. Check the variant on the scan.
